verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              हते वैकर्तने राजन् कुरवो भयपीडिताः । वीक्षमाणा दिशः सर्वाः पर्यापेतुः सहस्रशः ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said On Karna being slain, all the Kauravas, stricken with fear, fled away in all directions looking vacantly.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णं तु निहतं दृष्ट्वा शत्रुभिः परमाहवे । भीता दिशो व्यकीर्यन्त तावकाः क्षतविक्षताः ॥२॥
verses.english: Hearing that the heroic Karna had been killed by his enemy your soldiers, overcome with fear, fled away on all sides.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽवहारं चक्रुस्ते योधाः सर्वे समन्ततः । निवार्यमाणाश्चोद्विग्नास्तावका भृशदुःखिताः ॥३॥
verses.english: Your all warriors then suffering from anxiety and agony, had received a number of wounds on their bodies. Hence, they all scattered in all directions wherever, they got the way.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां तन्मतमाज्ञाय पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव । अवहारं ततश्चक्रे शल्यस्यानुमते नृप ॥४॥
verses.english: Then the Kuru leaders anxiously desired to rally your troops and your son also tried to cheek their flight.

verses.sanskrit: कृतवर्मा रथैस्तूर्णं वृतो भारत तावकैः । नारायणावशेषैश्च शिबिरायैव दुद्रुवे ॥५॥
verses.english: Encircled by the remaining portion of the Narayana troops Kritavarma speedily proceeded to his camp.

verses.sanskrit: गान्धाराणां सहस्त्रेण शकुनिः परिवारितः । हतमाधिरथिं दृष्ट्वा शिबिरायैव दुद्रुवे ॥६॥
verses.english: Seeing Adhiratha's son killed Shakuni surrounded by a thousand Ghandharvas, quickly returned to his camp.

verses.sanskrit: कृपः शारद्वतो राजन्नागानीकेन भारत । महामेघनिभेनानु शिबिरायैव दुद्रुवे ॥७॥
verses.english: Encircled by a large elephant force resembling a mass of clouds Saradvata's son Kripa quickly went towards his camp.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वत्थामा ततः शूरो विनिःश्वस्य पुनः पुनः । पाण्डवानां जयं दृष्ट्वा शिबिरायैव दुद्रुवे ॥८॥
verses.english: Sighing heavily at the success of the Pandavas, the brave Ashvatthama quickly went to his camp

verses.sanskrit: संशप्तकावशिष्टेन बलेन महता वृतः । सुशर्मापि ययौ राजन् वीक्षमाणो भयार्दितः ॥९॥
verses.english: Encircled by the remaining portion of the Samsaptakas which was still a large army, Susarma, looking at the terror-stricken' soldiers, went away.
Deprived of everything and his heart heavily laden with sorrow and afflicted by painful thoughts king Duryodhana went away.

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नध्वजेन शल्यस्तु रथेन रथिनां वरः । प्रययौ शिबिरायैव वीक्षमाणो दिशो दश ॥११॥
verses.english: Having his standard broken and looking on all sides, Shalya, the best of car-warriors, returned to his camp.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽपरे सुबहवो भारतानां महारथाः । प्राद्रवन्त भयत्रस्ता ह्रियाविष्टा विचेतसः ॥१२॥
verses.english: Assailed with fear and shame and beside themselves with grief the remaining car warriors of the Bharata army, still a large number, fled aw.y.

verses.sanskrit: असृक् क्षरन्तः सोद्विग्ना वेपमानास्तथातुराः । कुरवो दुद्रुवुः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा कर्णं निपातितम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Seeing Karna slain all the Kuru soldiers, trembling and with their voice suppressed with tears, fled away precepituously in fear.

verses.sanskrit: प्रशंसन्तोऽर्जुनं केचित्केचित्कर्णं महारथाः । व्यद्रवन्त दिशो भीताः कुरवः कुरुसत्तम ॥१४॥
verses.english: The great car-warriors of the Kuru army fled away in fear some praising Karna and other Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां योधसहस्राणां तावकानां महामृधे । नासीत्तत्र पुमान् कश्चिद्यो युद्धाय मनो दधे ॥१५॥
verses.english: Amongst the many thousand warriors of your army there was not a single individual who had any desire for fighting.

verses.sanskrit: हते कर्णे महाराज निराशाः कुरवोऽभवन् । जीवितेष्वपि राज्येषु दारेषु च धनेषु च ॥१६॥
verses.english: Upon the destruction of Karna, O king, the Kurus gave up all hopes of their lives, kingdom, wives and riches.

verses.sanskrit: तान्समानीय पुत्रस्ते यत्नेन महता विभुः । निवेशाय मनो दध्रे दुःखशोकसमन्वितः ॥१७॥
verses.english: Worked up with sorrow your son decided to give them rest for the night.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याज्ञां शिरसा योधाः परिगृह्य विशांपते । विवर्णवदना राजन्न्यविशन्त महारथाः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Obeying his orders, O king, the great carwarriors, bending low their heads, left the battle-field depressed and with pale countenances.
